title: Compute van der Waals constants
action: Using the reported polarizabilities α_I=5.6×10⁻²⁴ cm³ and α_Cd=2.4×10⁻²⁴ cm³, compute the van der Waals constants C_XX, C_XM, C_MM (in atomic units) via the Slater–Kirkwood formula.
description: Computes the van der Waals constants needed for the interatomic potential.
output_schema: object with keys: C_XX_au (number), C_XM_au (number), C_MM_au (number)

title: Compute Coulomb potential differences ΔVᶻ
action: Using effective charges z*_Cd=2z*, z*_I=-z* (z*=0.58) and lattice parameters a=4.244 Å, c=3.430 Å, γ=c/a=0.808, evaluate the analytic Coulomb potential differences ΔVᶻ_{ss'}(m) for distances m = 3/2, 5/2, 2 (XX and MM), and 3 (XX) via the leading exponential terms of the analytical Madelung-type formula.
description: Evaluates the Coulomb contributions to the interlayer potential differences.
output_schema: object with keys for each ΔV (e.g., ΔVz_XM_3/2, ΔVz_XM_5/2, ΔVz_XX_2, ΔVz_MM_2, ΔVz_XX_3) as numbers

title: Compute van der Waals potential differences ΔVᶜ by lattice sum
action: Perform numerical summation of the R⁻⁶ potential over a triangular lattice (up to ~2×10⁴ atoms per layer) for the distances m = 3/2, 5/2, 2, 3 using the van der Waals constants from step 0 and the lattice geometry. Obtain ΔVᶜ_{ss'}(m).
description: Computes the van der Waals contributions to the interlayer potential differences by direct lattice summation.
output_schema: object with keys for each ΔV_C (e.g., ΔVc_XM_3/2, ΔVc_XM_5/2, ΔVc_XX_2, ΔVc_MM_2, ΔVc_XX_3) as numbers

title: Compute repulsive lattice-sum coefficients for ΔVᵇ
action: Perform numerical summation of the R⁻¹² potential over the same triangular lattice for the same m values to obtain the linear coefficients f_{ss'}(m) such that ΔVᵇ_{ss'}(m) = B_{ss'} × f_{ss'}(m).
description: Computes the repulsive lattice-sum coefficients needed to express the Born–Mayer contributions.
output_schema: object with keys for each f coefficient (e.g., f_XM_3/2, f_XM_5/2, f_XX_2, f_MM_2, f_XX_3) as numbers

title: Compute exchange parameters (Coulomb only)
action: From the Coulomb ΔVᶻ values obtained in step 1, compute J₁, J₂, K using the relation that expresses these exchange parameters as linear combinations of potential differences. Save the results together with the ratios J₂/J₁ and K/J₁.
description: Exchange parameters computed when only the Coulomb part of the interlayer potential is included.
output_schema: object with number keys: J1_a.u., J2_a.u., K_a.u., J2_over_J1, K_over_J1

title: Compute exchange parameters (Coulomb + van der Waals)
action: Combine the Coulomb ΔVᶻ (step 1) and van der Waals ΔVᶜ (step 2) contributions, then compute J₁, J₂, K via the same relation as in step 4. Save the parameters and the ratios J₂/J₁, K/J₁.
description: Exchange parameters computed when both Coulomb and van der Waals parts are included (no repulsive term).
output_schema: object with number keys: J1_a.u., J2_a.u., K_a.u., J2_over_J1, K_over_J1

title: Derive frustration-line relation for Born–Mayer constants
action: Insert the full ΔV (Coulomb + vdW + repulsive with unknown B_{ss'}) into the frustration-line condition J₁−2J₂−K = 0. Solve for B_XM as a linear function of B_XX and B_MM, obtaining numerical coefficients α and β for CdI₂.
description: Derives α and β that define the linear relation among repulsive constants.
output_schema: object with number keys: alpha_a.u., beta_a.u.

title: Compute full exchange parameters and equilibrium bond length
action: Assume B_XX = B_MM = α (using α from step 6) and set B_XM = α. Evaluate the total ΔV (Coulomb+vdW+repulsive) using the coefficients from steps 1–3 to obtain the final J₁, J₂, K via the same relation as in step 4. Also compute the equilibrium Cd–I bond length R₀ from the condition dW/dR = 0 using the full pair potential W(R) with the chosen B_XM. Save all quantities.
description: Final exchange parameters including repulsion, the derived α and β, the assumed B values, and the equilibrium bond length.
output_schema: object with number keys: J1_a.u., J2_a.u., K_a.u., J2_over_J1, K_over_J1, alpha_a.u., beta_a.u., B_XX_au, B_MM_au, B_XM_au, R0_au
